business_problem: After the merger that created Virgin Media O2, the company needed to reduce siloed operations, legacy technology, and slow service experiences so it could resolve customer issues faster and deliver more personalized support across channels.
solution_summary: Virgin Media O2 and Accenture modernized customer service around a cloud-based digital core that unifies customer data across channels and applies AI directly inside service workflows. The foundation gives agents a connected view of prior conversations and similar cases so they can predict customer needs and identify the best resolutions more quickly. On top of that core, VMO2 uses Amazon Connect as an AI-powered contact-center service spanning voice, chat, and mobile interactions. Real-time tools listen to live conversations, suggest responses, surface a next-best-action banner with relevant offers, and guide agents through documentation with an AI-assisted flow tool. A unified desktop keeps those capabilities in one place, while identity controls protect customer and agent data. The result is an operating model in which data, contact-center AI, and workflow automation work together to reduce transfers, shorten wrap-up work, and improve the consistency of customer support.

data_flow: Customer interactions from voice, chat, and mobile channels feed into the cloud-based digital core, where prior conversations and related issue history create service context. Amazon Connect and associated AI tools use that context during live conversations to recommend responses and next actions, while the AI-guided flow tool and unified desktop help agents document and resolve the case in one workflow.
business_outcome: Virgin Media O2 improved service quality and efficiency, reduced complaint handling delays, gave agents better case guidance, and used AI-driven workflows to raise customer satisfaction while lowering administrative overhead.
